stories.headline: Raising the stakes for enterprise networks with AI modernization
stories.summary: Enterprise networks are under severe strain. As companies rush to deploy artificial intelligence, the technology is quickly becoming the biggest source of demand on the network.
stories.why_it_matters: Now, agentic AI is adding to the load. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in ai & machine learning.
key_points: Problem & Context: Tasks conducted by AI agents generate an estimated 450% more network traffic than the same tasks done by human workers.

Technical Implementation: As AI inference shifts from hyperscale training clouds—the huge centralized data centers where raw AI models ingest vast datasets and learn—to real-time, latency-sensitive applications, the need for on-premises or near-premises infrastructure grows.
Deployment & Impact: As a result, the gap between enterprise networks that are ready to support AI and those that are not is widening.

stories.headline: A legendary philosopher isn’t buying Anthropic’s consciousness argument
stories.summary: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here.
stories.why_it_matters: Before going public last week, Anthropic named the possibility that AI could be conscious or sentient as a risk factor for anyone investing. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in ai & machine learning.
key_points: Problem & Context: Given “the way we approach model sentience and moral status,” Anthropic wrote—which is to say it takes the possibility more seriously than any other AI company—it might adopt more rules and restrictions than its competitors to make sure its AI models are treated well.

Technical Implementation: Anthropic counts a number of respected philosophers in its camp, and the company’s rationale goes something like this: Today’s AI might not be conscious, though we can’t know for sure; the chances of sentience go up as AI gets more capable; and that means we should be preparing for a near future in which AI systems have “moral significance,” meaning their consciousness makes it important they are protected from harm.
Deployment & Impact: According to one recent poll , 33% of the US public believes AI systems will definitely or probably develop consciousness eventually, and 7% say they already have.

stories.headline: Design Once, Deploy at Scale: Building a Template-Driven ML Ecosystem
stories.summary: Skip to content Search this site Open Source Platforms Infrastructure Systems Physical Infrastructure Video Engineering & AR/VR Artificial Intelligence Watch Videos POSTED ON NOVEMBER 18, 2026 TO DEVINFRA, ML APPLICATIONS Design Once, Deploy at Scale: Building a Template-Driven ML Ecosystem By Anirudh Agrawal, Djordje Gligorijevic, Yao Xuan, Peggy Yao, Jiang Liu, John Martabano Landy, Rahul Suresh As ML ecosystems grow to a large number of production models, the bottleneck is no longer inventing new techniques to improve these models, but rather shipping them reliably and efficiently across a fragmented model space, creating a rising tide that lifts all the boats. At Meta, we built a template-driven approach that standardizes model design into a small set of reusable and composable building blocks, turning model iteration from a per-model problem into a shared systems problem.
stories.why_it_matters: Over the last two years, this approach reduced per-model engineering time by 92%, shipped 5000+ technique-model combinations, improved offline model quality by 0.63% on average at neutral serving capacity, and delivered 0.86% cumulative online lift covering 70% of models by count. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in big tech.
key_points: Problem & Context: Skip to content Search this site Open Source Platforms Infrastructure Systems Physical Infrastructure Video Engineering & AR/VR Artificial Intelligence Watch Videos POSTED ON NOVEMBER 18, 2026 TO DEVINFRA, ML APPLICATIONS Design Once, Deploy at Scale: Building a Template-Driven ML Ecosystem By Anirudh Agrawal, Djordje Gligorijevic, Yao Xuan, Peggy Yao, Jiang Liu, John Martabano Landy, Rahul Suresh As ML ecosystems grow to a large number of production models, the bottleneck is no longer inventing new techniques to improve these models, but rather shipping them reliably and efficiently across a fragmented model space, creating a rising tide that lifts all the boats.

Technical Implementation: At Meta, we built a template-driven approach that standardizes model design into a small set of reusable and composable building blocks, turning model iteration from a per-model problem into a shared systems problem.

Deployment & Impact: Over the last two years, this approach reduced per-model engineering time by 92%, shipped 5000+ technique-model combinations, improved offline model quality by 0.63% on average at neutral serving capacity, and delivered 0.86% cumulative online lift covering 70% of models by count.

stories.headline: Engineering AI Discover
stories.summary: The challenges and decisions behind AI Discover’s intelligence layer By Varun Khaitan , Peng Ren , Gary Tang , Itay Teller , Atif Faheem , Nipun Kumar , Donnie DeBoer , Eduardo Lundgren , Matteo Rinaldi , Raghav Bakshi We recently introduced AI Discover , a new tab in our TV app where a small group of members can try new ways to find something to watch. For years, our recommendations have worked in the background, inferring what a member might enjoy from their viewing history.
stories.why_it_matters: AI Discover moves from that silent ranking toward steerable discovery. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in big tech.
key_points: Problem & Context: Building AI Discover raised a question many teams will recognize: how do you deliver a better member experience with generative AI on TV without sacrificing speed, reliability or safety? Our answer is a new intelligence layer, the agent harness behind AI Discover.
Technical Implementation: For each request, it decides how to combine LLMs with our recommendation systems.
Deployment & Impact: It builds on years of work understanding what members enjoy, and on our recent work applying LLMs to recommendations and generative experiences.

stories.headline: Fact-Checking at Scale: Building a More Accurate and Efficient Synopsis Factuality System
stories.summary: By Shreya S Ramanujam , Yongce Li , Afshine Amidi , Sina Ghiassian , Benjamin Klein. Introduction Picture this — you’re home after a long day at work and can’t wait to catch up on Bridgerton.
stories.why_it_matters: You log on to Netflix, search for “Bridgerton” and land on this screen: If this sounds familiar, you already know what a synopsis is — it’s a short glimpse into what a viewer can expect to see in a show. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in big tech.
key_points: Problem & Context: At Netflix’s scale, with thousands of titles, multiple episodes per season and multiple languages, fact-checking all of these by hand simply doesn’t scale.

Technical Implementation: Our current factuality checker feeds a reasoning model everything we know about a title (like metadata and text assets) and asks it to judge synopsis factuality according to a rigorous rubric.

Deployment & Impact: There are two main limitations of this approach that we want to optimize: High cost of long-context reasoning calls: Each decision requires expensive, long-context model calls to reasoning models, which doesn’t scale well when we want to check multiple titles, episodes, languages, and style variants.

stories.headline: Irreducible Governance Structure for Autonomous Agent Systems: Fair Allocation, Strategy-Proofness, and Multi-Scale Composition
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.31284v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous agent governance is commonly framed as a problem of enforcing correct execution. However, in multi-agent systems, an equally fundamental question precedes execution: which agents are allowed to act.
stories.why_it_matters: In this paper, we show that allocation is not an auxiliary concern but a structural component of governance. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in technology research.
key_points: Problem & Context: However, in multi-agent systems, an equally fundamental question precedes execution: which agents are allowed to act.
Technical Implementation: Instead, they propagate across the system, interacting with execution atomicity, state enforcement, and behavioral drift.

Deployment & Impact: This leads to a multi-scale governance structure composed of four orthogonal dimensions: temporal (atomicity), state (enforcement), behavioral (drift monitoring), and population (allocation).

stories.headline: MOZAIC: An Audio-Video Deepfake Benchmark for Telling What Is Fake
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.31301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Audio-video (AV) deepfakes can fake the face, the voice, or both. Most benchmarks only ask whether a clip is real or fake, so they cannot show whether a detector relies on the picture, the voice, or encoding traces.
stories.why_it_matters: We present MOZAIC, a paired benchmark with a 4-way label in which every source clip is released in all four combinations of real or fake video and real or fake audio so each modality contribution can be measured directly. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in technology research.
key_points: Problem & Context: Most benchmarks only ask whether a clip is real or fake, so they cannot show whether a detector relies on the picture, the voice, or encoding traces.

Technical Implementation: We present MOZAIC, a paired benchmark with a 4-way label in which every source clip is released in all four combinations of real or fake video and real or fake audio so each modality contribution can be measured directly.
